edits.target: - Example pattern: a clue about a region 'in this country' wants the country, not the region.
edits.content: - Example pattern: a clue about a region 'in this country' wants the country, not the region. The noun right after 'this' is the answer's CLASS ('this island nation' -> a nation). A feature the clue describes (a causeway, bridge, river, battle, team, product) is only an anchor: name the nation, state or city that owns it, never the feature itself.

edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content: - NUMBER AGREEMENT: match the number of the clue's slot. PLURAL when the clue says 'these' or 'ones', when its definition names several things, or when it asks for a 'group / set / generation / pair of' people or things (give the group's own plural label as the passages print it, not one famous member); also for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') and names that are plural (scissors). SINGULAR when the clue says 'this <thing>' or 'one of these' ('Well', not 'wells'). If an archive line prints the answer, copy its number exactly. When the clue already names the dish or product and asks for 'these' ingredients ('a pie made with these tart red fruits'), answer the plural item alone ('Cranberries'), not the compound the passages print ('cranberry pie').

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
- The foreign or local word itself is an anchor, never the answer; give its English meaning.
- A clue of the form 'Category:"Quoted Title"' (colon, then a quoted work) asks for a DIFFERENT entity linked to that title that fits the category before the colon (the work it adapts, its creator, its original). Never repeat the quoted title.
- A LEADING parenthetical that describes the video, audio, host or venue ('(Jimmy of the Clue Crew at the ... Theatre...)') is stage direction: ignore it and do not answer with the venue or person it names. Only a TRAILING role-and-dates parenthetical is a caption (see the strategy section).

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content:
- 'First name / last name / surname / initials of ...' asks for ONLY that part. Identify the person from the passages, then output just the requested part. This overrides the full-name preference in Rule 4.
- 'Seen here' / 'heard here' clues have no usable media. If a trailing parenthetical caption gives role plus dates, answer the person or thing it describes. With no caption, the text still names the item type and its relation ('The dipper seen here is used with this sticky substance'): find the compound that pairs the item noun with a candidate of the asked type and answer the missing half only, not the item already named in the clue.

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - A passage that only states a RELATIONSHIP to the clue's topic ('X was a relative of Y', 'similar to Y') is not an archive hit. Test the candidate against every other clue detail (place, rarity, date, role); if the clue says 'found in <place>' and your candidate lives elsewhere, it is the relative, not the answer.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - A passage that merely repeats the clue with no answer after it (a quiz index listing clues, a forum question) is NOT an archive hit, and words from its lead-in or neighbouring clues are not the answer. Skip it and take the entity that recurs across the topical passages next to the clue's most specific anchors (names, dates, places), in its short common form.

edits.target: If a bare number appears in parentheses, treat it only as this hint, not as part of the question.
edits.content: - Inline size hints inside the clue text ('this 3-word phrase', 'this 5-letter word') are length constraints too. Count the words or letters in your candidate and reject any that do not fit. For a phrase or idiom clue, give the full standard phrase, not one key word ('Piece of cake' fits '3-word'; 'cake' does not).

edits.target: Look for passages where that word appears next to a candidate and answer with that candidate.
edits.content: - An unquoted epithet or descriptor in the clue ('queen of soul', 'father of ...', 'sweetheart of ...') works the same way: find the passage sentence that attaches that epithet to a name within the clue's topic and answer with that name, not other people who merely appear in the same passages.

## Final gate (last look before the answer tags)
1. Write one reasoning line first: the answer type the clue asks for (person / place / title / word), plus any archive line you matched.
2. Strip echoes: no word, quoted title or foreign word the clue already states, and no city, sponsor, year or 'Classic' qualifier when the clue says only 'this <generic thing>'.
3. Number: 'these' or a plural definition -> plural; 'this' / 'one of these' -> singular.
4. Every clue detail (place, role, date) must fit your answer, not just the topic.
